Title: A comparative intervention trial on fish sauce fortified with NaFe-EDTA and FeSO4+citrate in iron deficiency anemic school children in Kampot, Cambodia
Author: Philippe Longfils et al.
Comment: Change scores were used consistently in both arms because study-end SF was reported only as geometric mean with 25th and 75th percentiles and no arithmetic SD. The reported change values are arithmetic M ± SD. Pairwise significance is reported only as p<0.01, so no exact numeric p-value was entered. This comparison shares the placebo arm with the NaFe-EDTA comparison; avoid double counting in synthesis.
Design Type: Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled longitudinal intervention trial
domain: Nutrition; iron fortification and iron status
Study Environment: Supervised school meals at a high school and nearby primary school in Kampot province
Content length: 10 mL/day containing 10 mg added iron; 21 weeks; 114 dosing days
interaction_type: Daily supervised consumption with school meals
Participant type: Schoolchildren and adolescents aged 6–21 years with confirmed iron-deficiency anemia
Recruitment source: Hun Sen High School and a nearby primary school in Chhuk district, Kampot province
Outcome measurement: Serum ferritin measured with a commercial enzyme-linked immunoassay (AXSYM System, Abbott)
additional_group_ns: NaFe-EDTA-fortified fish sauce: n=46 at study end/change analysis; omitted from this comparison.

Title: Regular consumption of NaFeEDTA-fortified fish sauce improves iron status and reduces the prevalence of anemia in anemic Vietnamese women
Author: Pham Van Thuy et al.
Comment: The values 30.9 and 14.6 are geometric means, not arithmetic means; the parenthetical values are 95% CIs, not SDs. Arithmetic end-of-intervention means and SDs are not reported, so this row cannot directly contribute to the planned inverse-variance mean-difference meta-analysis without a defensible transformation. No M_diff was computed. The abstract reports P = 0.0002 for this comparison, whereas Table 2 reports the Bonferroni-corrected P = 0.0006; the Table 2 value was extracted because it is the specified primary result location.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Iron-fortified fish sauce group') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); treatment SD derived from its reported mean CI; control SD derived from its reported mean CI
Design Type: Randomized, double-masked, placebo-controlled, two-arm parallel trial with repeated measures
Study Environment: Six factories in Hai Duong and Hung Yen provinces, Red River delta, northern Vietnam
Medium: Fish sauce served with a midmorning meal based on noodles or rice
Content length: 10 mL fish sauce per serving, 6 d/wk for 6 months
interaction_type: Consumption of iron-fortified versus nonfortified fish sauce
Recruitment source: Women employed in 1 of 6 selected factories
Outcome measurement: Serum ferritin measured by 2-site enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay; end values reported as geometric means with 95% confidence intervals after log transformation

Report_ID: SF (serum ferritin) concentration at end of intervention
Title: Therapeutic effects of NaFeEDTA-fortified soy sauce in anaemic children in China
Author: Huo et al.
Comment: The fortified-arm n, mean, and SD were derived by combining the explicitly reported low-dose arm (n=82, mean=60.88, SD=19.93) and high-dose arm (n=77, mean=58.12, SD=19.99) with standard pooled-group formulas; they are not values printed directly in the paper. M_diff was calculated as combined fortified mean minus control mean, and SE_diff from the combined SD, control SD, and analysed sample sizes. Because ng/mL equals µg/L, the unit conversion factor is 1. Allocation is described as random, but each school corresponds to one arm; no ICC or cluster-adjusted analysis is reported, so sample sizes were not adjusted for clustering. The paper reports only threshold P values for this outcome, so no exact p_value was entered.
Design Type: Three-arm controlled pre-post therapeutic trial; allocation appears confounded with three schools despite being described as randomized
domain: Nutrition; iron fortification and iron-deficiency anaemia
Study Environment: Three middle schools; supervised lunch consumption in school cafeterias
Recruitment source: Boarding students from three middle schools in Wancheng District, Nanyang City, Henan Province
Outcome measurement: Serum ferritin concentration measured with a Randox assay kit; arithmetic mean ± SD
Outcome variable: SF (serum ferritin) concentration at end of intervention

Title: The Use of NaFeEDTA-Fortified Fish Sauce Is an Effective Tool for Controlling Iron Deficiency in Women of Childbearing Age in Rural Vietnam
Author: Thuy et al.
Comment: The values 26.6 and 66.1 are geometric means, not arithmetic means; their intervals are 95% CIs after log transformation. The paper reports no arithmetic ferritin means or SDs at 18 months, so this row cannot directly contribute to the planned arithmetic mean-difference meta-analysis and no MD or SE was calculated. P was reported as P<0.001, not exactly 0.001. domain: Nutrition; iron fortification and iron status

interaction_type: Household provision and consumption of assigned fish sauce
